MOLECULAR PATHOLOGY REPORT

Received: [redacted date]
Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL HISTORY
Adult female with lung adenocarcinoma. Tissue submitted for MET gene analysis to evaluate eligibility for targeted therapy.

TEST PERFORMED
MET Gene Status by Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH)

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue sections using the GeneTech DualProbe MET/SE7 assay. This probe set includes a red fluorophore targeting the MET gene locus at 7q31 and a green fluorophore targeting the chromosome 7 centromere (7cen). A total of 60 tumor cell nuclei were evaluated. MET amplification status was assessed using both MET/7cen ratio and absolute MET copy number criteria as per published guidelines (Cappuzzo et al., J Clin Oncol 2009).

RESULTS
MET/7cen ratio: 1.07
Mean MET copy number per cell: 2.40
Mean chromosome 7 centromere signals per cell: 2.24

INTERPRETATION
MET FISH NEGATIVE

The tumor shows no evidence of MET gene amplification by FISH analysis. Both the MET/7cen ratio (1.07) and mean MET copy number (2.40) fall below the thresholds for positivity. MET amplification is defined as MET/7cen ratio ≥2.0 or mean MET copy number ≥5.0 per cell.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
This patient's tumor is MET FISH negative, indicating the patient is unlikely to derive clinical benefit from MET tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as crizotinib, cabozantinib, or capmatinib in the context of MET amplification.

RECOMMENDATIONS
MET-targeted therapy is not indicated based on these FISH results. Alternative molecular profiling including comprehensive genomic profiling may be considered to identify other actionable alterations in this non-small cell lung cancer.

Electronically signed by:
[redacted name], MD, PhD
Board Certified in Molecular Genetic Pathology
